finalText:
**Merge** takes two branches and combines them with a new commit that has both as parents. It keeps the full story — you see exactly when branches split and came back together. It's safe with others because it doesn't change the commits that already exist.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, as if you'd written them there from the start. It rewrites history, but the result is one clean line. It's best on commits you haven't shared yet.

Use **merge** when you want to keep the history intact, you're combining finished features, or you're working with other people on the same branch. Use **rebase** before you push, to clean up a messy local history and keep the main history easy to read. Never rebase commits someone else is depending on — the rewrite breaks their branch.

The tradeoff: merge is honest and safe, rebase is clean but requires discipline. Most teams merge to main and rebase locally.
